newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine Airline warns striking pilots.
newsitem.headline: Philippine Airline warns striking pilots.

text.p: Philippine Airlines (PAL) on Sunday warned it would fire pilots who joined any illegal walkout in an attempt to head off a second strike in a month in the financially-troubled national air carrier.
PAL management said issues the pilots had raised in talks with the company were now in the hands of labour department arbiters and any stoppage at this point would violate the law.

"The management ... will not hesitate to fire anyone who joins any illegal action that would disrupt company operations while the labour dispute between PAL and the Airline Pilots Association of the Philippines (ALPAP) is under conciliation," it said in a statement.

The 600-strong ALPAP said on Saturday its members were considering going to the picket lines "anytime" in protest against the dismissal of two senior pilots and unfair labour practices. It also said PAL was using its financial losses as an excuse for a wage freeze.
Management said the pilots were also demanding a 15 percent annual salary raise for the next five years.
PAL's ground staff struck on October 31 in a dispute over a new wage package but returned to work after three days. It was the third strike to hit the cash-strapped carrier in two years.
